q: Is my chlor-alkali plant covered by India's carbon credit trading scheme?
title: Is a chlor-alkali plant covered by CCTS?
short: Only if it is named. Chlor-alkali was in the first round of emission intensity targets under the 2025 target rules, but coverage is plant by plant. Electricity for electrolysis is the largest part of a caustic plant's emissions, so captive power records decide the number.
audience: Caustic soda and chlorine producers in India

ol: Find the Greenhouse Gases Emission Intensity Target Rules, 2025 and any amendment.
Search the chlor-alkali schedule for your plant name and location.
If listed, note the baseline year, product unit and target for each compliance year.

ul: Electricity per tonne of caustic from cell room meters, by source: grid, captive coal or gas, and renewable.
Fuel for the captive plant and for caustic concentration or flaking.
Production of caustic, chlorine and hydrogen, read from dispatch and stock records.

p: You have no target, but obligated customers may ask for your energy and emissions data, and the offset mechanism lets non-obligated entities earn credits from projects under methodologies BEE has approved.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and production documents into dated, fingerprinted plant records, so the monthly intensity behind a compliance figure can be traced to its source.
